tutorial.title: Keeper's Handbook
tutorial.page1.title: Controls: Strike and Hold
tutorial.page1.body:
Move with WASD / arrow keys; dash with Space; interact with E; open the codex with C.

The mouse sets your attack direction. Hold-click to attack continuously; a single click performs one tool attack and is briefly buffered until the weapon is ready. Press X to toggle auto attack: auto mode aims at the nearest enemy without requiring a held mouse button. The HUD shows Manual / Auto.

Esc pauses or closes a panel. Upgrade cards stay locked for their first 0.2 seconds.
tutorial.page1.note: The short arrow beside your character shows the actual aim direction, not a damage cone. Blades and impact effects show collision feedback.
tutorial.page2.title: Culture: Ningcun to Yongchang
tutorial.page2.body:
In 1386, Tang He oversaw the construction of Ningcun fort. In 1558, Wang De moved to Ningcun to support the defense and died at Jin'ao the next day; the Wang family later built Yongchang Fort.

In 1559, Wang Lu (A-Liu) is a fictional lamp-watch militia, not Tang He. This game turns coastal-defense memory into a night watch.

The codex separates history, institutions, folklore, and dramatization, with sources for each.
tutorial.page2.note: Historical references: records in the Wenzhou Prefecture Gazetteer and Yongchang Fort: Thirteen Jinshi and the Anti-Wokou Chronicle. Wang Lu is a fictional character.
tutorial.page3.title: Systems: Hold Until Dawn
tutorial.page3.body:
In manual mode, hold left-click and each weapon fires when ready. Defeating enemies grants XP immediately; choose one weapon, passive, formation, or skill when you level up. Empty oil means darkness: +50% experience, but faster enemies and less visibility—a risk-and-reward choice.

The market opens every 120 seconds for weapons, equipment, and retinue. Five dragon scales trigger a field clear; the counter then resets for a new cycle. Explore the outer map for encounter sites: green icons usually bring allies or buffs, red icons may spring ambushes, slow you, or hasten the enemy surge. The minimap marks them. Survive 16 minutes, defeat the boss, and meet the dawn.
tutorial.page3.note: Upgrade cards stay locked for 0.2 seconds. Replay this tutorial any time from pause or the main menu.
tutorial.page4.title: Attributes: Read the Watch HUD
tutorial.page4.body:
Start at the upper-left HUD: health reaching 0 ends the watch. Empty oil causes darkness: gain 50% more experience, but enemies move faster and visibility shrinks. The market opens every 120 seconds; spend coins on weapons, gear, and allies.

The selection screen shows each post's attributes. Balanced Wang Lu starts with 140 health, 154 movement speed, 88 pickup radius, and 6 oil. His saber deals 15 damage, swings every 0.58 seconds, reaches 126 units, and covers a 118° arc. These values serve different jobs: damage sets each hit, a shorter interval attacks faster, range measures distance from the player to the hit area, and arc sets its width.

Defeat enemies to gain XP, then choose one of three upgrade cards. Passives change attributes; weapon upgrades can evolve. Watch impact flashes and knockback when attacks connect. Use Space to escape pressure; do not judge a build by damage alone.
tutorial.page4.note: These figures describe the Balanced Post at run start; other posts, upgrades, and gear change the HUD. See Settings → Controls for live bindings.

codex.cards.title: Hero Codex · Wang Lu's Watch Posts
codex.cards.lead: All six hero portraits are Wang Lu, taken from the first CharacterForge idle frame of each post. Only the kit, post, and footwork change; these are not six people.
codex.cards.disclaimer: Wang Lu is the fictional 1559 lamp-watch militia A-Liu; Tang He appears only in the 1386 prologue.
codex.cards.source: Post role: {role}; gameplay is a project dramatisation.
codex.cards.allies_lead: Recruit in the market, up to three. Allies are marked by a green ring underfoot.
codex.cards.read_more: Click a hero portrait for the full dossier.
codex.upgrades.title: One-of-Three Upgrade Codex
codex.upgrades.lead: Every card that can appear in a level-up draw: attributes, skills and formations, outer encounters, and tower works. Values show level 1; open a card for its full notes and cultural background.
codex.upgrades.summary: {cards} card types · {offers} total upgrade levels in the pool
codex.upgrades.rule: Maxed cards leave the draw; encounter cards appear at most once per run.
codex.upgrades.detail_rule: The one-of-three draw selects from attribute, skill, encounter, and tower pools by rarity and current level. Maxed cards no longer appear, and an encounter card can appear only once in a run. Card faces show level 1 values; actual upgrades stack by level.
codex.equipment.title: Gear Codex
codex.equipment.lead: Carried gear comes from the lamp market; trait cards come from the one-of-three upgrades. Values reflect the current build.
codex.weapons.title: Weapon Codex
codex.weapons.lead: Seven base weapons across five attack shapes; five evolve with matching gear, while the Folangji and command banner are complete from the start.
codex.weapons.source: Source: One-of-three upgrades / Lamp Market weapon slot
codex.enemies.title: Enemies / Elites
codex.enemies.lead: Common raiders, ranged and support troops, then dragon-scale elites from 2:00 and the daimyo at 15:30.
codex.enemies.source: Source: tide combat data; values scale with difficulty.
codex.maps.title: Maps / Encounters
codex.maps.lead: Beyond the central arrow tower lie outer encounters. Take the reward, then survive what follows.
codex.maps.encounters_lead: Encounters can grant allies, merit, healing, or stats; they can also summon elites, waves, and temporary slows. Each event appears at most once per run.
codex.maps.encounter_source: Source: Outer encounter point / one-of-three event
codex.history.title: Fort History & Background
codex.history.lead: This second-layer cultural record stays out of the default combat codex.
codex.history.deep_lead: Five close readings: garrison institutions, a clan-built fort, lamp-lit night work, dragon-lantern custom, and the distinction between two temples. Each entry is marked as historical record, institution, local custom, or dramatisation.
